paragraphs.text: Dear elders and sisters, well, we're now on day four of our new reality.

I have been swamped with issues from the evacuation, but soon most of the evacuated missionaries will be home. They will be placed in a 14-day isolation, and then the ones who are close to being finished with their missions will be released, and the ones who still have lots of time left to serve will be reassigned to serve in a mission in their home country.
We've already heard from the few who have made it home. They are heartbroken about leaving the mission and wish they could return to finish their missions here with us.

I understand their sadness, but life hands each of us challenges and obstacles, and our job is not really to feel sorry for ourselves, but to actually feel gratitude for our challenges. Because by embracing them, we can grow and become better, smarter, and stronger.
The assistants and I are working hard to get all the functions of the mission back up and running. Our senior couples really did so much work, but now we need to do it.

One piece of very good news, though, is that Elder and Sister Cross, while down at the MTC with the other returning missionaries, had a strong feeling and desire to return and serve with us. And we're able to get the permission from the Missionary Department, and so they're now back in the mission and helping us get back on track.

Each of you should have received by now your new ward assignments. The stake presidents, when I told them about our plan, were so excited. They all have the names, phone numbers, and Messenger names for each missionary serving in their stake, and they also know which wards the missionaries are assigned to serve.

When you get your assignment, you will also get the bishop's name and phone number. I would ask that you'd quickly reach out to him, introduce yourself, help him to know that you are his servant, and you're there really to help him bless and strengthen the members of his ward.
These bishops are really fine men. They do a great work, and they do it without pay. At the same time, they also have to take care of their own families and jobs.

Many of them will be struggling with their own challenges, and so you can be a strength to the bishop. Be patient with him and with the members. Many of them are struggling with many challenges and stresses. Be kind and loving, always ready to provide an uplifting comment and never taking offense.

Keep building your skill with online video presenting. I simply cannot tell you how valuable this will be in these next few weeks to the members and also in the future for you. The missionary who gets really good at communicating online has the best of all options available for them in the future professional world.
When you do your best for the Lord, He will pay you now and forever. And this is one way you can see that happen now and in the future in your profession.
Now some of you may be feeling a little stress yourselves. This is normal.

Whenever it gets a little too much, just stop and sit down or lay down and do this simple breath exercise. Take a deep breath in through the nose and then hold it for about 10 seconds. And then slowly let it out through the mouth while quietly saying to yourself, "Relax. Let go. Relax."

Do this at least five times and you will cause what is called the relaxation response in your body and mind. The more you do it, the more you train your body to relax. Just when you command it to relax: let go, relax.
This skill can be learned by anyone, and I consider it to be one of the most important skills I've ever learned. A relaxed mind and body can function so much better than one that is tense and tight.
So relax. Let go. Relax. Each time you release that air, you'll find yourself having more power, more clarity, more calmness, and more ability to function with energy.
Now finally, I have to remind you to maintain missionary standards.

It will be very easy to slip into bad habits: not getting up on time, not getting dressed in missionary attire, not performing proper grooming and hygiene, and not being actively engaged in the work of salvation, which is the work of serving someone other than yourself.

When you choose to not do what you know you should do, you are choosing to live a lie. A person who gets comfortable living a lie will become a very unproductive and unhappy person. They will get into a place that's very hard to get out of.
So discipline yourself and make it unnecessary for others to have to discipline you. Be your own boss, and the world will find you and give you all kinds of rewards and opportunities.
Now a word about the phones. This is a sacred privilege. We must be exactly obedient to the rules we all agree to for using the smartphones and practice the safeguards for using technology.
Review those safeguards on the Missionary Portal and also the other resources there about protecting yourself as you use technology.
I trust you, and yet I know that there might be a few missionaries who think that they can get away with breaking this rule or that rule.
Elders and sisters, honor your word. Be men and women of integrity.

While you may hide the breaking of a rule from me or even from your companion, you will never hide it from God or yourself. You will always know that you either were a person of integrity or you were not. And that will either be a powerfully positive image you will carry with you or a powerfully negative one.
At the end of our lives, we will find that the only personal possession we will have is that personal integrity.
I love you.
I'm proud to serve with you.
Let's go make a difference today.
